overview_markdown:
grip-ai is a self-hostable AI agent platform written in Python (~24,000 lines, 120+ modules) that positions itself as a lightweight OpenClaw alternative. Its architecture is built around a dual-engine design: the Claude Agent SDK serves as the primary engine for Claude models, while a LiteLLM-based engine provides fallback to 15+ other providers including OpenAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Gemini, and local options like Ollama, vLLM, and LM Studio. Notably, grip bridges its full 31-tool registry into the SDK engine as in-process MCP tools, so both engines expose the same tool surface — filesystem, shell, web search, Playwright browser automation, document conversion, and more.

Reliability is a clear focus: the project implements automatic retries with exponential backoff, true cross-provider failover via litellm.Router with per-deployment credentials, and per-call USD cost tracking with daily totals. It supports multi-channel chat over Telegram, Discord, and Slack, cron scheduling, multi-agent orchestration, and a REST API, all from a single `grip gateway` process. Code quality practices are unusually rigorous for a project this size — 882 tests, ruff linting, and a mypy-clean tree enforced in CI as of v1.6.1.

Compared to OpenClaw, grip-ai trades ecosystem maturity for a leaner, Python-native codebase that is easy to read and modify. However, it lacks documented sandboxing for its shell and browser tools, has no meaningful community adoption yet (11 stars, no real Reddit discussion), and depends heavily on a single maintainer. It is best suited for developers who want a hackable, multi-provider agent platform and are comfortable vetting the security model themselves.
